title: The Beggar King
text: An old man in a paper crown begs at a crossroads in the otherworld, his robe stitched from banners nobody flies anymore. He once ruled all of this, he says, and points at the ruins as if they were still standing. He holds out his cup to the House that has least.

options.label: The poorest House drops what it can into his cup, knowing what it is to have little.

outcomes.text: He blesses them in a voice once used to giving orders. For a moment, the ruins stand tall.
He takes it with a laugh. For a moment his crown is gold, as is the gift he gives back.

options.label: The richest House laughs at his paper crown. A king of nothing deserves no bow.

outcomes.text: He bears it with dignity and only nods. Something in the ruins of his kingdom remembers your faces.

options.label: The wisest asks about his kingdom, curious what could have brought it so low.

outcomes.text: He tells it well, with tears in his eyes. Some of it is even true.
